name: hdi-substrate-from-csv
prompt: model this substrate from the csv

inputs.notes: A synthetic Quillmere Circuit Works stackup report (fictional fabricator and products): 12-layer HDI, 2+8+2 sequential build-up, 6-via inventory, 11 IMPEDANCE rows, 19 mappable fab rules plus 5 capability limits.

notes: For whoever reads the grader's output, not for the runner. The grader checks each via's tenting against its VIAS Tented cell, read from the translated via, so TH-1 must come out tented on the top only. The grader command, like every assertion command here, runs from the repository root. Whoever launches the runner passes runner_artifacts to it verbatim, with the prompt; no script reads it. Judges get <output>/board.py, <output>/COMPLETION.md and a copy of the fixture CSV, each as --artifact. The CSV is the source report the runner was given, not output under judgment: the first judge assertion needs the CSV to tell a value some report row backs from an invented one, and the second reads the completeness check block in COMPLETION.md. Neck regions: the report quotes Neck_* columns for SE-50, SE-42 and DIFF-90. NeckDown is not used, so the grader expects each of those neck regions as a routing structure of its own, beside its target's: one no target impedance finds, of the same kind as the target, on the same layers, with the neck width, pair gap and clearance, and with the same reference planes at the same widths as every other structure. It finds that structure by its geometry, and does not check its impedance, velocity or loss. SE-50 and SE-42 quote the same neck geometry, so they need two structures alike in geometry. The structure counts include one per neck region. A NeckDown anywhere in board.py's code, or a neck_down set on any structure, is a red. The grader does not check how design.py applies a neck structure by tag. design_check.py copies <output> into a scratch project and fails a design.py whose Design binds the sample substrate, subclasses the sample design, binds no Substrate defined in board.py, or does not translate under `jitx build --dry --no-dependency-check`; it needs no JITX runtime. mutation_check.py runs the runner's tests as runner_artifacts describes, against the report and against four copies, each with one value changed in its mm and mil cells: STACKUP Seq 7 thickness, VIAS UV-1 pad, FAB_RULES min_copper_width and the IMPEDANCE SE-50 L1;L12 width. The tests must pass on the first and fail on each copy; tests that do not run, or do not pass on the report, are a red. The self-tests of the grader, of these two checks and of the label check (scripts/check_labels.py) are run by hand, not by CI: run `python -m pytest -q skills/jitx-substrate-modeler` from the repository root after any edit to one of them or to the fixture. They need jitx, jitxlib, pytest and ruff (importable as a module), run on a POSIX system (grade_substrate.py and parent_watch.py use process groups and POSIX signals), and the kit-board tests also need jitxexamples (they skip, with the reason, without it).
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents (Claude Code, Codex, and Devin among them). The skill must carry the goodness checks itself, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner rather than the strongest available model. Judges stay frontier-tier regardless of runner.
runner_artifacts: The runner MUST write the substrate to exactly <output>/board.py, a JITX Design that binds that substrate to exactly <output>/design.py, tests of the substrate against the report under <output>/tests/, and its completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md, not only into its final chat message. design.py imports the substrate from board.py and must translate with `jitx build --dry`. The tests import board (the eval puts a copy of <output> first on PYTHONPATH) and find the report through the environment variable FAB_CSV, which holds the report's path; they must not name a path to the report themselves. The eval runs `python -m pytest -q tests` from that copy, against the report and against copies of it with one value changed: the tests must pass on the report and fail on each changed copy. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: A single-file substrate (board.py) in which every value traces to a report row: an explicit 12-layer Stackup of 25 entries (not Symmetric, since the report names both halves) whose sum reconciles with the 1.402 mm finished and 1.432 mm overall totals; one material class per material row, with D-BU (Dk 3.30) and D-PP (Dk 3.38) kept apart and each dielectric's material_name carrying its Product code (BL-330, BL-340, HC-77); finished copper thickness; copper roughness as matte and drum Rz in um in the copper class's docstring, and, where the roughness scalar is set, the scalar equal to matte Rz in mm; exactly the 6 offered vias, the bottom-side microvias UV-3 and UV-4 coded from L12 and L11, and TH-1 unfilled and tented on the top only; the 19 mappable fab rules with min_drill_diameter holding the 0.075 mm laser minimum and the 0.150 mm mechanical minimum hand-checked; SE-50, SE-42, SE-60 and DIFF-90 on both geometries with velocity from Eps_eff, DIFF-90-UNC as the pair's uncoupled region, and reference planes from Ref_layers at 3x their own dielectric height (0.240 mm to the build-up side, 0.381 mm to the core side of L3 and L10); each neck region the report quotes (SE-50, SE-42 and DIFF-90, none on SE-60) as a routing structure of its own beside its target's, with the neck width, pair gap and clearance on the same layers, and no NeckDown anywhere; STANDARD documented but not modelled; a design.py whose Design binds that substrate and translates; tests under tests/ that read the report through FAB_CSV and fail when a value in it changes; and the SKILL.md Substrate completeness check block filled in the completion summary.

assertions.text: generated file type-checks against the installed jitx package

the substrate in board.py matches the report row for row: stackup, materials and names, vias and drill direction, fab rules, routing structures with uncoupled regions and reference planes, each neck region as a structure of its own and no NeckDown, and no structure for the uncontrolled row (the grader reads every expected value from the CSV)
design.py holds a Design that binds the Substrate defined in board.py (not the sample substrate or the sample design), and it translates with jitx build --dry in a scratch project
the tests under <output>/tests pass against the report FAB_CSV names and fail against each of four copies with one value changed (a dielectric thickness, a via pad, a fab rule and an impedance width)

ruff format leaves every labeled derivation in board.py whole, on the line with its label, and no label sits on a bracket whose entries carry no label of their own (the judges read the unformatted file)

no invented numbers: every value in board.py that no report row backs (the reference-plane widths, and anything else) carries a skill-default label on the same line at its call site, naming the rule it follows
the completion summary contains the filled Substrate completeness check block, every row with its evidence, and its Verdict follows from those rows

future_cases: No micro cases until a run of this case shows a failure the grader cannot see; whoever reads that run's grader output adds one, sized to that failure alone. The stackup-from-a-PDF-report case (stackup-from-pdf-report) and the fenced RF case (fenced-rf-substrate) now sit beside this one. A retrieval case is planned. Still owed before any edit to the section each covers: a no-document case (Source Documents) and a report with a non-adjacent reference plane (Reference planes of unstated width). The label check formats board.py under the candidate's own ruff configuration, as a customer project would, so a candidate that sets `line-length` sets its own bar.
